component.name: Arctis Sound Manager
component.summary: Linux GUI for SteelSeries Arctis headsets

description.p: Arctis Sound Manager is a Linux application for configuring SteelSeries Arctis headsets. It provides a 4-channel audio mixer (Game / Chat / Media / HDMI), a full Sonar parametric EQ system, virtual 7.1 surround sound, and device management.
Features:

ul.li: 4-channel audio mixer with automatic media routing
Sonar EQ — parametric EQ with 297+ presets, Spatial Audio, Smart Volume
Micro processing — AI Noise Cancellation, Noise Gate, Compressor
ANC / Transparent mode control from GUI and headset
Virtual 7.1 surround via HeSuVi HRTF convolution
Device status — battery, mic mute, sidetone

description.p: Quitting ASM no longer crashes when PipeWire stops answering (#349). The tray's last default-sink switch could time out and the error killed it before it finished; a unit that ignored the stop was then sent a second polite signal instead of being killed. Both are handled now. Thanks @ziggityzack for the reproduction and the analysis. ASM no longer re-sends the same move to an idle native app every 5 seconds (#349). An app pinned to an output but not playing has no link, so ASM never saw it as already there and asked PipeWire again and again for the whole session. It now asks once per stream. Arctis Pro (2019, wired) gets a profile of its own, audio only. It was handled as a wireless Arctis 7, whose commands it does not have, so its battery, ChatMix and headset settings never worked. Like the Arctis 5 (2018), it now gets the audio features (channels, Sonar EQ, spatial audio) and no controls that would do nothing.

Arctis GameBuds: choose the audio source, the 2.4 GHz dongle or Bluetooth, the switch GG makes when its EQ panel changes tab. On Bluetooth, this computer's audio through the dongle no longer reaches the earbuds. Not yet tried on real GameBuds. Arctis 7 / 7 2019 and Arctis 1 Wireless / 1X / 7X / 7P: microphone volume, as GG offers it (0-100). Not yet tried on hardware: if you own one, please tell us on #331 whether it works. Arctis Nova Pro Wired: line out, stream mix and screen dimming. Line out to speakers or streaming, the main / aux / mic stream mix, and when the GameDAC's screen dims, as GG offers them. Not yet tried on a real one: if you own one, please tell us on #331 whether each control works.

Nix: the package builds again on recent nixpkgs (#344). nixpkgs switched Python packages to structured attributes in October, which passed each grouped wrapper option as a single argument that makeWrapper rejected. Each argument now stands on its own. Contributed by @jgopel. Apps go back to their channel when the dongle or headset comes back (#343). When the channels disappear (dongle unplugged, headset off), every app falls back to another output, and on reconnect only the apps you had pinned to a channel came back; a game left on Game stayed on the monitor speakers. ASM now remembers which channel each app was on and puts it back, without touching an app you have since moved to another ASM channel. Thanks @Fabi0699. Nova Pro Omni: the base station's own screen flashed over ASM's custom display (#330). ASM drew all 64 rows, over the 12-row status strip at the top that the base keeps for itself; each time its charging indicator changed, the Omni redrew its whole screen for up to a second. ASM now draws 128x52 below that strip, as GG does on this family (the Nova Elite too). Thanks @FrDrebin for tracking it down to the charging battery.

The headset's own settings are on the Headset page. Sidetone, mic volume, volume limiter, sleep timer, ANC and the rest of what your model supports moved out of Settings, where they sat among the app's options, onto the Headset page: one card per group, next to the live status, shown as tiles. Settings keeps ASM's own options, in cards too, and neither page scrolls sideways any more. The Sonar tabs are joined to the panel they control, and the Micro tab gets the input picker the other tabs already had. Contributed by @Denkiyaa (#333). Arctis Nova Pro Wireless: ASM starts from what the base station already has. Line out, the stream mix, mic volume, sidetone, gain, Bluetooth, the mute-LED brightness, the sleep timer and the wireless mode are read from the base station before ASM sends anything, so a setting you never changed in ASM keeps the value it had (set in GG or on the DAC) instead of being reset to ASM's default. Also new: the base station's home screen view (detailed or simple). Confirmed on hardware with asm-cli tools probe. Windows owners can record what SteelSeries GG sends to their headset (#337). scripts/reverse-engineering/capture-gg-windows.ps1 finds the SteelSeries device plugged in and walks through that model's own settings in GG, one at a time, while USBPcap records; the result shows ASM exactly what each setting expects on that model. See #337 for the steps.

asm-cli tools probe. Asks the headset for its state with read-only queries — the ones SteelSeries' specification lists for that model, nothing that changes a setting — and saves the raw replies to ~/asm-probe.json. One file from an owner is enough to check how a model reports its settings, instead of one question per setting in an issue. Custom EQ and the base station settings on the Arctis Nova Pro Omni. The Omni's base station runs the same firmware family as the Elite and takes the same commands, so it now gets what the Elite already had: the Equalizer page's *Switch to Custom EQ*, the on-ear microphone sidetone, the line out (speaker or stream, with the stream mix volumes), and the screen's screensaver, its timeout and the home screen view and options. Written from SteelSeries' specification and not yet confirmed on a real Omni — Omni owners, please try it and report on #330. Arctis 7: sound cut out while the log filled with "USB error: Overflow" (#317). The dongle can get stuck sending status frames larger than its USB endpoint allows, on every read, for hours; the sound came back only once ASM was quit. ASM now resets the dongle once when this lasts a few seconds, the way it already recovers a headset whose commands all fail, and logs the error every hundred reads instead of twice a second. Thanks @kevinhu12345 for the logs.

Custom EQ on the Arctis Nova Elite. The Elite's own equaliser, inside the headset, can now be driven from the Equalizer page (*Switch to Custom EQ*), like the other models with an on-device EQ; the curve stays on the headset. Written from SteelSeries' specification and not yet confirmed on a real Elite — Elite owners, please try it and report on #327. No Sonar audio on SteamOS: the permission repair removed permissions instead of granting them (#325, #181). ASM passed the permission to pw-cli as letters (rwxml), which pw-cli reads as the number 0, so every attempt to unblock a refused link took the remaining access away and made the refusal worse. It now sends the numeric value and reads the permissions back to check they took effect. Thanks @rasmus91 and @baccatuesday for the logs. GameBuds charging case not shown, "Access denied" in the log (#217). The 1.6.0 package from the pacman repository shipped empty udev rules, and ASM's own check did not notice: it ignored the charging case's product ids and accepted any complete copy of the rules, even one hidden by an older copy in /etc. The package build now fails instead of shipping empty rules, and the check looks at the file udev actually reads, so ASM rewrites outdated rules by itself. Thanks @Sev501.

Streamer mode. Like Sonar's Stream mode in GG: a second, independent mix of Game, Chat, Media, Aux and the processed Mic, each with its own volume and mute, delivered as a "<device> Stream Mix" source for OBS or any recorder. Turn it on with the Streamer mode switch next to the Channels menu and every card gets a compact Stream slider and mute button. The mix is taken before your headphone volumes and EQ/spatial audio, so viewers hear the clean game (7.1 is downmixed to stereo with the dialogue kept), and your headset mix and ChatMix are unaffected. Off by default; toggling it restarts the filter-chain once (short audio dropout, same as switching a preset), volume and mute changes are live. GameBuds charging case. With the case plugged into the computer over USB, the Headset page shows its battery, charging state, lid (open/closed) and which earbuds are seated in it, like GG. The case is read next to the dongle, never instead of it: plugging or unplugging it leaves your audio alone. Arctis Nova Pro Wired: fixes for the volume knob cutting the sound, maxing the volume, killing the mic or lagging (#321). Thanks @TheV-git for the detailed report. ASM was talking to the wired DAC in the Nova Pro Wireless base's language: it polled a settings frame and set a mic-mute LED level that the wired DAC does not have, which it refuses with a Pipe error in the log. Those two commands are gone (the mic-mute LED brightness slider with them), and the daemon now asks for the wheel position instead. The OLED is drawn the way SteelSeries' own app does it (below the DAC's status area, in the report size the spec gives) and handed back to the DAC when ASM stops. The daemon also reads the knob's reports as fast as they come instead of ten a second. These changes follow SteelSeries' specification but are not yet confirmed on this DAC: if the knob still misbehaves, please comment on #321.

Automatic Sonar preset per game. Turn on "Automatic preset per game" on the Sonar page and ASM applies the matching Game channel preset as soon as a game starts (Steam, Lutris, Heroic or by executable name), like GG's QuickSet. A preset you pick by hand while the game runs is remembered for that game. The tray menu lets you force a preset for the running game or choose "Do not change". Off by default; switching preset restarts the filter-chain (short audio dropout, same as GG). The OLED screen shows the EQ of what you are listening to. The EQ line used to always show the Game preset; it now follows the channel actually playing (Media, Chat, Output…) and is labelled with its name. A Discord call never takes it over from a running game. Bug reports include the kernel's USB and sound messages, from the current and the previous boot, so a report made after rebooting still shows what went wrong. (#317).

Mic card on the Channels page. A new card on the far left sets the volume of what your apps record, picks which microphone feeds it (same choices as Settings) and shows which apps are recording. (#315). See where each channel plays. Every channel card now shows the name of its output device under its buttons, without opening the picker. (#316). Hide any card. The Channels menu now lists every card (Mic, Master, Game, Chat, Media, Aux, Output), so you can keep only the ones you use. Hiding a card only removes it from the page; the channel keeps working.

Real 7.1 for Game, Media and Aux. These channels now accept 5.1/7.1, so a game set to surround sends its real centre and rear channels instead of a stereo mix. Spatial Audio (HeSuVi) now places those real channels around you; a stereo app still plays exactly as before. Surround passthrough to speakers. A channel sent to a 5.1/7.1 receiver or TV gets its channels as they are, with no headphone rendering. A 5.1 receiver that only has side or rear surrounds gets the other pair folded in instead of losing it. Clean stereo downmix. With Spatial Audio off on a stereo device, surround content is folded into stereo (centre and surrounds at -3 dB) instead of keeping only the front left/right, which used to drop a 7.1 game's dialogue.

DAC Wheel Overlay. Turning the volume wheel on the base station / GameDAC floats a "DAC wheel" bar at the bottom of the screen, in the same place as the ChatMix bar (now called Chat/Mix Overlay). Can be turned off in the settings. Arctis Pro Wireless: spare battery and base station screen. The spare battery charging in the base is shown on the Channels page, and the base's OLED can be used from the DAC page. Arctis Pro Wireless battery stuck at 50% (#305). ASM read the radio link state instead of the battery; it now reads the real battery level.

Headset disconnecting every couple of minutes (#299). When a headset stopped answering commands, ASM reset its USB connection after every failed initialisation, so it kept dropping and reconnecting, interrupting audio. ASM now tries the reset only once; if that does not help, it leaves the device connected and logs that it needs a replug or power cycle.

ChatMix on-screen display. Turning the ChatMix dial (or the mixer page's bar) floats the ChatMix bar at the bottom of the screen for 1.5 s, above the taskbar and over fullscreen games. Works on KDE and wlroots Wayland (layer-shell), X11, and GNOME Wayland (through a small bundled GNOME Shell extension). On by default, can be turned off in the settings. Plasma 6 widget. Shows the headset power state and battery, the base station's spare battery, noise cancelling and microphone state, and opens asm-gui. It is fed by a new StatusChanged D-Bus signal emitted by the daemon, so it no longer needs to poll. Its strings are translated through Crowdin. OLED: now-playing line. The base station / GameDAC custom display can show "Artist - Title" of the playing MPRIS player, with a marquee.

asm-cli status shows the headset state: battery, power, mic and. Drag an application onto a channel card to move it, from its icon on. New documentation pages: SteelSeries headsets on Linux, one page per.
